what: Validation-methodology correction (2026-04-26): when testing whether content is being INJECTED into agent context (vs available via tool calls), do NOT test in the same chat where tools were already called — prior tool-call results carry forward in conversation history and confound the test. Use a FRESH chat/session in the same project, and ask about content UNIQUELY in the injection source (e.g. rules-file body) and NOT in any seeded memory. The "Do NOT store: obvious facts, temporary state, secrets, trivial observations" line in shared/body.md is a good isolation probe — it appears only in rules content, never as a memory. Same-session "write a function" tests are weak signals because the agent may apply guidelines from earlier tool-call results, not from injection. This applies to validating any session-start-injection workaround (Cursor C4 rules-file regen, future similar workarounds for other editors) and any test of "does agent's context include X" claims.
why: User pushed back on my proposed "write a getUser function" test (2026-04-26): it wouldn't isolate rules-file injection from prior-turn tool-call context, since the agent already had memories in conversation history from the previous Scenario N call. Real test needs fresh session + content unique to the injection source. Storing as a project-wide guideline scoped to validation work so future validation runs (other editors, future workarounds) start from the right methodology rather than re-discovering the confound.
